title: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
description: Shredded raw green papaya pounded in a mortar with chilies, lime, and long beans until it weeps its dressing — sour, hot, and crunchy in the same bite. This version swaps fish sauce for soy and mushroom seasoning to keep it fully plant-based.

image.alt: Shredded vegetable salad with peanuts in a dark bowl on stone

ingredients: 2–4 Thai bird's eye chilies, to taste
1/4 cup long beans, cut into 4cm lengths
1 tsp mushroom seasoning powder (or an extra pinch of salt)
steps: In a large mortar, pound the garlic and chilies to a coarse paste.
Add the palm sugar and pound to dissolve, then add the long beans and bruise them lightly.
Add the tomatoes and bruise just enough to release their juice — don't pulverize them.
Add the shredded papaya in two batches, bruising and turning with a spoon between each addition (not pounding hard, or it turns mushy).
Add the lime juice, soy sauce, and mushroom seasoning. Toss and taste — it should hit sour, salty, sweet, and hot all at once.
Transfer to a plate and scatter with crushed peanuts.
note: Choose papaya that's fully green and firm — a ripening papaya turns the salad soft and sweet instead of crisp.
